findings.passage: To help protect Indiana's elections, officials will have more tools to maintain accurate and up-to-date voter registration lists. Also, proof of citizenship will be required for individuals registering with temporary IDs and first-time voters will be required to provide proof of residency.
findings.note: Caucus press release issued in her name (Rep. Patterson highlights new laws effective July 1, 2024). Under the heading 'Increasing Election Security' she lists new laws on voter-roll upkeep, proof of citizenship for people registering with temporary IDs, and proof of residency for first-time voters.
subjects: proof of residency for first-time voters

findings.passage: A new law ensures only government-issued IDs are accepted at election polls and that voter rolls are properly maintained to remove inactive and deceased voters. It specifies that student IDs, which cannot be used to register to vote, are not an acceptable form of identification at polling places.
findings.note: Caucus press release issued in her name (Patterson highlights new state laws now in effect, July 30, 2025). Under the heading 'Ensuring Election Integrity' she lists a new law limiting polling-place ID to government-issued IDs, excluding student IDs, and requiring removal of inactive and deceased voters from rolls.
subjects: accepted ID types at polling places

findings.passage: "This new text hotline is another great tool for Hoosier voters," Patterson said. "Whether it's checking your polling times and location, or asking about election security, this resource can help."
findings.note: Joint caucus release with other area legislators about a state election text hotline run by the Secretary of State's office. Related to election security and voter help, not to ID rules directly.
